features.name: New canvas and canvas initialization
steps: Handle the save confirmation while unsaved content exists
The tools, colors, and canvas return to a state where editing can continue
features.expected: After New the canvas is blank and editable; the confirmation flow for unsaved content triggers correctly; the tools/colors return to their initial usable state.

features.name: Open a local image
steps: Choose a supported local image such as PNG/JPEG/BMP/GIF/WebP
Load the image onto the canvas
The canvas size fits the image and all drawing tools can continue to be used; the official JS Paint also supports several bitmap formats and some TIFF/PDF/SVG/ICO input formats. GitHub
features.expected: The loaded image must fit the canvas and be editable with all drawing tools; the canvas size matches the image.

features.name: Save and Save as
steps: Choose the file name and image format
The image content matches the saved state
features.expected: After saving and reopening the exported file, the image content matches the saved state; the file name and format are correct.

features.name: Automatic backup / Manage Storage
steps: Let the page keep an automatic backup after editing the image
The previous image is restored; the official JS Paint documentation states that a backup of the current image is kept automatically and managed through Manage Storage. GitHub
features.expected: Manage Storage must list recoverable records; after reloading, the previous canvas is restored.

features.name: Undo / redo
steps: Draw, fill, create shapes, or perform image transformations in succession
Undo steps back through several operations
Each step's image changes correctly according to the history
features.expected: Undo steps back several steps in reverse history order; redo restores; each step's image changes correctly according to the history.

features.name: History
steps: Perform several different operations in succession
Then jump to a later or different branch
The canvas restores the corresponding state; JS Paint supports a non-linear, nearly unlimited undo history. GitHub
features.expected: History must show the operation history; after jumping to an earlier state or branch the canvas restores the corresponding state.

features.name: Cut / copy / paste
steps: Create a rectangle or free-form selection
Place it at a new position
The canvas content updates according to cut or copy semantics
features.expected: Cut/copy/paste semantics are correct; a pasted selection can be moved and placed at a new position.

features.name: Copy To / Paste From
steps: Copy To saves the selection as a separate image
Paste From selects another local image
The image enters the current canvas as a floating selection
After positioning it is merged into the image. GitHub
features.expected: Copy To must save the selection as a separate image; Paste From loads an image as a floating selection that can be merged.

features.name: Select all and delete the selection
steps: The whole canvas becomes the selection
The unselected states and operation results are correctly preserved
features.expected: After select-all the whole canvas becomes the selection; after moving/deleting, the selection is cancelled and the result is correctly preserved.

features.name: Free-form selection
steps: Select an image region along an arbitrary outline
The selection contains only the pixels inside the hand-drawn outline
features.expected: A free-form selection must contain only the pixels inside the hand-drawn outline; after dragging, only the selected content moves.

features.name: Rectangle selection
steps: Drag out a rectangle on the canvas
After dropping the selection the content is merged at the target position
features.expected: The rectangle selection is created and moved correctly; the transparent/opaque modes take effect; after dropping it merges at the target position.

features.name: Selection copy-dragging and stamp-style copying
steps: Place the same content several times
The original image is kept or moved with correct semantics; JS Paint also supports classic Paint behaviors such as Shift-drag smearing and Shift-click "stamping". GitHub
features.expected: Copy-dragging can place the same content several times; the source image changes correctly according to move/copy semantics; the Shift behavior matches classic Paint.

features.name: Crop to the selection
steps: Create a rectangle or free selection
The canvas size shrinks to the selection range
Pixels outside the selection are removed; JS Paint also supports holding Ctrl to create a selection for cropping. GitHub
features.expected: After cropping the canvas size shrinks to the selection range; pixels outside the selection are removed.

features.name: Eraser
steps: Erase the passed area to the background color
After changing the size the erase width changes in sync
features.expected: The eraser only erases the passed area to the background color; after a size change the erase width changes in sync.

features.name: Color-replacement eraser
steps: Set the foreground and background colors
Use the eraser and right-drag over a specific color region
Only pixels matching the foreground color are replaced with the background color
Other colors stay unchanged, which is classic Paint behavior supported by JS Paint. GitHub
features.expected: The right-click color-replacement eraser only replaces pixels matching the foreground color with the background color; other colors stay unchanged.

features.name: Paint-bucket fill
steps: The whole connected region is filled with the color
Tapping different areas only affects the corresponding connected region
features.expected: The paint bucket only fills the connected region that was tapped; different regions do not affect one another.

features.name: Whole-image color replacement fill
steps: Set the target color and the replacement color
Replace all non-contiguous regions matching the color across the image rather than only one connected region. GitHub
features.expected: Shift-click must replace all non-contiguous regions matching the color across the whole image.

features.name: Eyedropper color picking
steps: Tap an existing color on the canvas
Then use the pencil, brush, or fill tool
The new content uses the sampled color
features.expected: After picking with the eyedropper the foreground color updates; subsequent drawing uses the sampled color.

features.name: Magnifier
steps: Choose a zoom level such as 1×, 2×, 6×, or 8× in the tool options
Tap the image to zoom in
Switch the zoom level or zoom out
The edited content stays unchanged and only the view scale changes
features.expected: The magnifier switches scales correctly; only the view scale changes and the edited content stays unchanged.

features.name: Pencil
steps: Choose the foreground color from the palette at the bottom
Continue drawing after switching the color
Existing strokes keep their original color
features.expected: The pencil produces continuous single-pixel-style lines; after switching colors new strokes use the new color while old strokes stay unchanged.

features.name: Brush
steps: Choose a different brush width or tip from the tool options
Produce strokes of the corresponding width
Continue drawing after changing the color and tip
features.expected: The brush's different widths/tips are applied correctly; drawing continues correctly after switching.

features.name: Airbrush
steps: Hold the mouse button and move
The longer the dwell time in a region the higher the color density
features.expected: The airbrush produces random speckled spray; the longer the dwell time the higher the density.

features.name: Text tool
steps: Drag out a text box on the canvas
Choose the font, size, bold, italic, underline, etc. in the font toolbar
The text is rasterized into the image after completion
features.expected: The text styles (font / size / bold, italic, underline / transparent background) are applied correctly; it is rasterized into the image after completion.

features.name: Line tool
steps: Drag from the start point to the end point
Change the width and color and draw again
New straight lines use the corresponding settings
features.expected: The line tool's width and color are applied correctly.

features.name: Curve tool
steps: Drag out a basic straight line
Then drag the segment to control the curvature
The curve color and line width follow the current settings
features.expected: The curve tool controls curvature correctly; the color and line width follow the current settings.

features.name: Rectangle tool
steps: Set the outline/fill combination and line width
Test outline-only, outline+fill, and fill-only separately
The shape style matches the selection
features.expected: The rectangle outline/fill combinations are correct (outline only / outline+fill / fill only).

features.name: Polygon tool
steps: Return to the start point or double-tap to finish
Render according to the current outline and fill mode
features.expected: The polygon is created vertex by vertex and closed; it renders according to the current outline/fill mode.

features.name: Ellipse tool
steps: Toggle the outline and fill modes
Supports different color combinations and line widths
features.expected: The ellipse is created correctly; the outline/fill mode and color are correct.

features.name: Rounded-rectangle tool
steps: Toggle the fill/outline style and color
New shapes use the current style in sync
features.expected: The rounded rectangle is created correctly; the style and color are applied in sync.

features.name: Foreground color / background color
steps: Left-click a color in the bottom Color Box to set the foreground color
Right-click to set the background color
Use the drawing or shape tool to verify the two colors
Both color boxes display the selection in sync
features.expected: Left-click sets the foreground color and right-click the background color; both color boxes display in sync; drawing verifies correctly.

features.name: Third color slot
steps: Hold Ctrl to choose the third color
Press or release Ctrl during drawing
Switch between the third color and the normal color immediately in the current strokes. GitHub
features.expected: Ctrl The third color must switch and take effect immediately in the strokes.

features.name: Edit the custom color
steps: Define a custom RGB/HSL color from the color picker
The custom color can continue to be selected
features.expected: The custom color must be added to the palette and remain usable.

features.name: Palette import / export
steps: Get Colors loads a palette file
The Color Box updates to the imported color
Save Colors exports the current palette; the official app supports multiple palette formats such as PAL, GPL, ACO, and ASE. GitHub
features.expected: Palette import/export is correct (PAL/GPL/ACO/ASE); the Color Box updates after importing.

features.name: Flip / Rotate
steps: Create a selection or apply to the whole image
Choose horizontal flip, vertical flip, or a rotation angle
The current selection or the whole image is transformed according to the settings; JS Paint also allows an arbitrary rotation angle. GitHub
features.expected: Flip/rotate applies to the selection or the whole image according to the settings; arbitrary-angle rotation takes effect.

features.name: Stretch / Skew
steps: Enter the horizontal/vertical scale percentages and the horizontal/vertical skew angles
The current selection or the whole image is scaled and sheared according to the parameters. GitHub
features.expected: Stretch/Skew correctly scales/shears by the entered percentage and angle.

features.name: Invert Colors
steps: Apply Image to the whole image or the selection
Every pixel is converted to its inverse
The original colors are restored; the official documentation explicitly supports applying inversion to the selection or the whole image. GitHub
features.expected: Invert must convert all pixels to complementary colors; undo restores it.

features.name: Image properties / Attributes
steps: Change the canvas width, height, and units
Switch between color/black-and-white mode or the transparency property
The canvas size and color/transparency mode update accordingly; transparent images can also be enabled here. GitHub
features.expected: Attributes correctly updates width/height and the color / black-and-white / transparency modes.

features.name: Clear Image
steps: When the canvas already has content
The whole canvas returns to the background state
features.expected: Clear Image clears the canvas to the background state; undo restores it.

features.name: Draw Opaque / transparent-selection mode
steps: Create a selection containing a background color
Toggle the Draw Opaque state in Image
When enabled the background color is covered too; when disabled the background-color area is transparent
Toggle again to verify the difference
features.expected: The Draw Opaque toggle must determine whether the background color covers when moving a selection; the two states must be verifiably different.

features.name: Tool Box display control
steps: The toolbox is restored while the current tool and canvas content stay unchanged
features.expected: The Tool Box shows/hides correctly; the current tool and canvas content are unchanged.

features.name: Color Box display control
steps: The palette is restored while the current foreground/background colors are preserved
features.expected: The Color Box shows/hides correctly; the foreground/background colors are preserved.

features.name: Status Bar display control
steps: The status bar is restored and continues to show contextual information such as coordinates and selection size
features.expected: The Status Bar shows/hides correctly; contextual information such as coordinates is displayed correctly.

features.name: Text Toolbar
steps: The text preview and the final pixel result change in sync; the current JS Paint provides this View menu item. GitHub
features.expected: The Text Toolbar shows/hides correctly; font/size changes affect both the preview and the final pixels.

features.name: Zoom menu
steps: Use standard zoom, magnified zoom, custom zoom, or Zoom To Window
The canvas is displayed at the target zoom
The edited content and the real image dimensions stay unchanged; the official app supports arbitrary custom zoom and fit-to-window. GitHub
features.expected: Zoom levels and custom/fit-window work correctly; the edited content and real dimensions are unchanged.

features.name: Grid display
steps: Zoom the view to a higher level
The grid disappears while the image stays unchanged; the classic Ctrl+G grid behavior is supported by JS Paint. GitHub
features.expected: The grid shows/hides correctly at high zoom; the image stays unchanged.

features.name: Thumbnail
steps: A whole-image thumbnail preview window appears
Pan or zoom on the main canvas
The thumbnail still provides the whole-image context
The main editing state is preserved after closing
features.expected: The Thumbnail provides a full-image preview; panning/zooming keeps the context; the editing state is preserved after closing.

features.name: Full-screen mode
steps: The editor occupies the browser's available full-screen area
The tools and canvas continue to work normally
Exiting full screen returns to the original layout. GitHub
features.expected: In full-screen mode the tools and canvas work normally; exiting restores the original layout.

features.name: Moving the canvas and scrolling
steps: Zoom the image beyond the visible area
Pan the view with the horizontal/vertical scrollbars or mouse/touch
Draw in different areas of the canvas
The original image coordinates and existing pixels stay consistent
features.expected: After zooming, scrolling/panning is correct; the original image coordinates and existing pixels stay consistent.

features.name: Resize via the canvas edges
steps: Drag the resize handles on the edges or corners of the white canvas
The newly added area uses the background color
The existing pixels keep their original relative positions
features.expected: The canvas edge handles correctly enlarge/shrink the canvas; the new area is the background color; the original pixels keep their relative positions.

features.name: Menu and shortcut linkage
steps: Perform Undo, Redo, Select All, Zoom/Grid, Save, etc. via the menu and the corresponding keyboard shortcuts respectively
Both entry points produce the same state change
The menu's disabled/enabled state updates in sync with the context
features.expected: The menu and keyboard shortcuts must produce the same state changes; the disabled/enabled states sync with the context.

features.name: Theme switching
steps: Switch between themes such as Classic, Modern, and Dark
The toolbox, menus, and window appearance change
The current image, colors, and editing history stay unchanged. GitHub
features.expected: Theme switching changes the UI appearance; the current image, colors, and editing history stay unchanged.

features.name: Language switching
steps: The menus, tooltips, and window text switch language
The current feature layout stays consistent. GitHub
features.expected: After switching languages the UI text changes correctly; the feature layout stays consistent.

features.name: Vertical Color Box
steps: Switch the horizontal bottom palette to a vertical layout
Restore the classic Color Box position
The color state is preserved. GitHub
features.expected: The Vertical Color Box switches layout correctly; the color state is preserved.

features.name: Quick Undo Button
steps: Show a touch-friendly floating undo button
Tap the floating button to undo
The button disappears after disabling the option. GitHub
features.expected: The Quick Undo Button floating button displays/undoes/closes correctly.

features.name: Render History As GIF
steps: Complete a series of drawing steps
Generate an animation from the document's editing history
The animation replays the image changes along the operation process. GitHub
features.expected: Render History As GIF must produce an animation replaying the operations; the saved GIF is correct.

features.name: Help / About
steps: Help Topics opens the usage instructions
View the tool or menu help
About Paint shows the JS Paint version/project information
Closing the window returns to the previous editing state
features.expected: Help / About opens the instructions and version information correctly; closing it returns to the previous editing state.

features.name: Complete drawing workflow
steps: Fill the closed region with Fill
Create shapes with Line, Curve, Rectangle, Polygon, Ellipse, and Rounded Rectangle
Open it again to verify the output
features.expected: The complete drawing workflow is correct at every step; after exporting, reopening verifies a consistent output.

exclusions.reason: Requires integrating the external Imgur service and network upload capability, which does not affect JS Paint's core local drawing, editing, and export workflow; the official documentation explicitly treats it as a web extension feature. GitHub

exclusions.feature: File → Load From URL / the cross-origin proxy behind pasting a URL
exclusions.reason: Local Open should be fully implemented; however, loading arbitrary public URLs may require a CORS proxy, and the official deployment documentation also notes an optional dependency on CORS Anywhere, so the reproduction can exclude cross-origin proxies and arbitrary web-image fetching. GitHub

The current implementation depends on Firebase, and the official documentation itself describes the feature as a rather rough experimental multi-user collaboration; it is not part of the classic Paint core editing experience. GitHub

exclusions.feature: Advanced accessibility controls such as Head Tracker / Speech Recognition / Dwell Clicker
exclusions.reason: These are extra features in Extras for special devices or browser capabilities such as eye tracking, head tracking, and voice control; full mouse, keyboard, and touch editing is enough. GitHub

exclusions.feature: File → Set As Wallpaper writing a real OS wallpaper
exclusions.reason: A browser page cannot reliably set the desktop wallpaper directly, and the official interface itself allows degrading to saving an image, so actually changing the user's OS wallpaper is not required. GitHub

The current goal is to reproduce the jspaint.app web version; Electron file associations, system menus, command-line startup, installers, PWA installation, and native desktop integration are not required.
